device.category: 4-voice paraphonic analogue synthesizer with 37-key keyboard, chorus, distortion, sequencer and arpeggiator
device.based_on: Moog Minimoog Model D, extended to four oscillators assignable one per note. The guide never names Moog; the controller, oscillator bank, mixer, ladder filter and contour layout, the decay switch and the keyboard control switches are the Minimoog's.

architecture.signal_path_note: analogue voice; the chorus is a BBD (bucket brigade) circuit and the distortion analogue; digitally scanned keyboard and sequencer
architecture.polyphony_mode: paraphonic: four oscillators assigned one per note in POLY, all four on one note in UNISON, or one note in MONO, sharing one filter and one pair of contours
architecture.summary: A four-oscillator Minimoog. Each oscillator has six ranges from LO to 2' and six waveforms; oscillators 2 to 4 have a frequency offset of plus or minus 7 semitones, and oscillator 4 can be freed from the keyboard to act as a modulator. In POLY mode each new note takes the next oscillator, so four notes play through a single 24 dB/octave ladder filter (low-pass or high-pass) and a single loudness contour: paraphonic, not polyphonic. A mixer with on switches blends the four oscillators, pink or white noise and an external input. Modulation is the Minimoog's: a mix knob between OSC 4 or the filter envelope and noise (or an external source) or the LFO, scaled by the mod wheel and switched onto the oscillators and filter. Then distortion, a BBD stereo chorus, a 32-step sequencer with 64 pattern memories, and an eight-mode arpeggiator. Velocity and aftertouch keyboard with CV outputs.

modules.name: Keyboard and MIDI
modules.description: 37 semi-weighted full-size keys with velocity and aftertouch, pitch and mod wheels, and MIDI in over DIN and USB. Transposes by an octave either way. Produces note, gate, trigger, velocity and aftertouch, all also available as CV.

modules.name: Voice assignment
modules.description: Assigns notes to the four oscillators, using logic Behringer says it adapted from the Korg Mono/Poly. MONO: every oscillator that is switched on plays one note. UNISON: the oscillators are shared among the notes held, all four on one note, two each on two, one each on four. POLY: the first note takes OSC 1, the next OSC 2, up to four. Key priority and multi-trigger are SysEx settings. AUTO DAMP decides whether released chord notes keep sounding until the next note.

modules.name: Tune, glide and bend
modules.description: Master tune, glide (switchable on the left of the keyboard), pitch wheel and the external OSCILLATOR CV, applied to the oscillators' pitch. OSC 4 is exempt from all of it when OSC 4 CONTROL is off.

modules.name: Oscillator 1
modules.description: Analogue VCO with six ranges (LO to 2') and six waveforms. The pitch reference; no frequency offset.

modules.name: Oscillator 2
modules.description: Analogue VCO with six ranges (LO to 2') and six waveforms. Frequency offset of plus or minus 7 semitones.

modules.name: Oscillator 3
modules.description: Analogue VCO with six ranges (LO to 2') and six waveforms. Frequency offset of plus or minus 7 semitones.

modules.name: Oscillator 4
modules.description: Analogue VCO with six ranges (LO to 2') and six waveforms. Frequency offset of plus or minus 7 semitones. Can be released from the keyboard and used as a modulation source, like the Minimoog's third oscillator.

modules.name: Noise
modules.description: Pink or white noise into the mixer, and the default modulation source.

modules.name: LFO
modules.description: Triangle or square, 0.05 to 200 Hz. A modulation source; also shown by a rate LED.

modules.name: Modulation mix
modules.description: The Minimoog modulation scheme. One switch picks OSC 4 or the filter envelope, another picks noise (or whatever is in MOD SOURCE) or the LFO. MODULATION MIX crossfades between the two, the mod wheel sets overall depth, and the OSCILLATOR MODULATION and FILTER MODULATION switches send the result to the oscillators and the filter.

modules.name: Mixer
modules.description: Volume and on switch for each of four oscillators, external input and noise. Overload LED on the external input.

modules.name: Filter
modules.description: 24 dB/octave ladder filter, switchable low-pass or high-pass. Cutoff, emphasis (resonance) and amount of contour; keyboard tracking in thirds by two switches; modulation from the mix bus; external CV at 1 V/octave.

modules.name: Filter contour
modules.description: Attack, decay and sustain shaping the cutoff. Release follows decay when DECAY is on.

modules.name: Loudness contour
modules.description: Attack, decay and sustain shaping the VCA. Release follows decay when DECAY is on, otherwise it is immediate.

modules.name: VCA
modules.description: Single amplifier for all four notes, opened by the loudness contour and the LOUDNESS CV input.

modules.name: Distortion
modules.description: Drive, tone and level, switchable in or out. Described by Wikipedia and owners as derived from the Boss DS-1 circuit, and by Sonic State as Neutron-style; unlike the Neutron, TONE has no effect without some drive.

modules.name: Chorus
modules.description: BBD stereo chorus with two modes, usable together, closely modelled on the Juno-60 chorus (an owner compared the two directly); the stereo spread is reportedly wider than the Juno's. Mono in, stereo out. The low -16 dBu main output level is attributed by owners to the chorus stage.

modules.name: Sequencer
modules.description: 32-step note sequencer (four pages of eight), 64 patterns in 8 banks of 8. Per-step gate length, tie, rest, accent, glide and ratchet (1 to 4 repeats); swing per pattern. Keyboard recording or step editing. Runs on the internal tempo or external sync.

modules.name: Arpeggiator
modules.description: Arpeggiates held notes in eight orders, with hold, at the sequencer tempo.

modules.name: Tempo and sync
modules.description: Internal tempo from TEMPO/GATE LENGTH, or external clock from DIN, USB or the SYNC IN jack. Clock rate and polarity for the jacks are SysEx settings. SYNC OUT carries the internal clock.

modules.name: Output
modules.description: Master volume and headphone volume; stereo main outputs after the chorus.

led_legend.rule: Two colour systems. The sequencer's LOCATION LEDs use colour for what they are showing: green in keyboard mode and for pages, patterns and saving; yellow in step mode and for ratchet counts; red for gate length. In step editing, individual LOCATION LEDs flag step properties: 5 glide, 6 ratchet, 7 accent, 8 rest. Separately, the backlit panel switches are coloured by function group: orange for signal on/off (mixer sources, distortion, chorus), teal for the filter, white for pitch and modulation routing and the DECAY switch, green for voice mode, yellow for the chorus modes.

exceptions: The backlit switch groupings (orange, teal, white) are read from the panel photograph and are not documented.

behaviours.name: Paraphonic, not polyphonic
behaviours.rule: In POLY mode each new note takes the next oscillator: one note plays OSC 1, two notes OSC 1 and 2, up to four. All four share one filter, one filter contour, one loudness contour and one VCA. The contours retrigger on new notes (multi-trigger is on by default), so chords play through a single envelope. The specifications call this '4 voices polyphonic'.

behaviours.name: Auto damp
behaviours.rule: Off: releasing some notes of a chord leaves them all sounding until every note is released or a new one played. On: released notes stop and only held notes continue. This exists because the shared envelope cannot release notes individually.

behaviours.name: Minimoog modulation bus
behaviours.rule: Two switches pick a source each (OSC 4 or filter contour; noise/MOD SOURCE jack or LFO), MODULATION MIX crossfades them, the mod wheel sets depth, and two switches send the result to the oscillators and the filter. Setting OSC 4 to LO, freeing it with OSC 4 CONTROL off and selecting it here makes it a second LFO, as on the Minimoog.

behaviours.name: Decay switch
behaviours.rule: The contours are attack, decay, sustain. With DECAY on, release takes the DECAY TIME; off, release is instant. Minimoog behaviour, applying to both contours.

behaviours.name: Keyboard tracking in thirds
behaviours.rule: Two switches: neither for no tracking, 1 for a third of full, 2 for two thirds, both for full.

behaviours.name: Effects chain
behaviours.rule: After the VCA: distortion (drive, tone, level; DS-1 derived) then a BBD stereo chorus modelled on the Juno-60, with modes I, II or both. The chorus turns the mono voice into the stereo output. The order is inferred from the panel and one owner's presumption; Behringer has not documented it.

behaviours.name: Sequencer
behaviours.rule: Up to 32 steps in four pages of eight, 64 patterns in 8 banks. Per step: note, rest, gate length 1 to 8 (8 ties), accent, glide and ratchet 1 to 4. Per pattern: swing, from off-beats only through straight to on-beats only. Keyboard mode records; step mode edits but cannot save until switched back. Live, SHIFT with the same controls applies ratchet, swing, mute or accent to the whole pattern without saving.

behaviours.name: Arpeggiator
behaviours.rule: Eight orders (up, down, down and up, random, and up or down with an octave added or removed), at the TEMPO rate, with HOLD to latch. Order is changed with <KYBD and STEP> while playing.

behaviours.name: Clocking
behaviours.rule: Clock source is internal, DIN, USB or the SYNC IN jack, at 1, 2, 24 or 48 PPQ, rising or falling edge; all SysEx settings with defaults of internal, 24 PPQ, rising. MIDI clock is sent to DIN and USB by default.

behaviours.name: Calibration
behaviours.rule: Each oscillator has RANGE and SCALE trimpots on the rear panel, tuned at A5 and A2 against a tuner with the instrument warm for 30 minutes, plus an octave-range trimpot matched by ear at C6. The wheels and aftertouch have a firmware calibration mode reached at power-on.

behaviours.name: POLY needs the oscillators switched on
behaviours.rule: Because POLY hands each note to a specific oscillator, a note assigned to an oscillator whose mixer switch is off is silent. For full four-note chords all four oscillators must be on; owners describe this as the most common surprise with the instrument.
behaviours.note: From Sweetwater owner reviews; follows from the guide's description of POLY.

source_inconsistencies: The specifications describe '4 voices polyphonic'; the controls describe one filter, one pair of contours and one VCA, so the instrument is paraphonic.
The specifications list 'Amount of contour' under the loudness contour; the panel and controls have no such control there.
SysEx packet 0x1A lists '1 PPS', read as 1 PPQ alongside 2, 24 and 48 PPQ.
SysEx packet 0x0F gives the MIDI transpose default as [1], while its note says 12 is no transpose.
Item 14 says TUNE adjusts oscillators 1 to 4; the specifications give it as -2 to +2 and the getting-started chapter says the TUNE and OSC 2 to 4 FREQUENCY knobs are marked in semitones.
Item 25 says OVERLOAD warns about the EXT IN volume; the Spanish text says it shows the mixer overloading.
The sequencer control list numbers 1 to 15 restart the main numbering, and the item for SEQUENCER (35) points to pages 15 and 38, which are not where the sequencer chapter is.

The guide describes UNISON only by name; Wikipedia and Sonic State describe it as dividing the oscillators among held notes, while Sweetwater's support article says it triggers all oscillators that are on, which matches only the single-note case.

modelling_gaps.detail: A Minimoog ladder with a Behringer-added high-pass mode. No cutoff range, resonance law or self-oscillation statement.
How the shared contours respond to overlapping notes depends on multi-trigger and auto damp; the exact rules for legato chords are not documented.
Frequency offsets are marked in semitones; the knob law between the marks is not given.
Distortion and chorus are described only by their controls. Retailers describe the distortion as modelled on a Boss DS-1; not in these sources.
No Minimoog documentation was supplied; it would settle the filter, contour curves and oscillator behaviour.
